consolidation_proposal.title: Session isolation guard: never write outside the session's own working folder (hard ACL long-term + single-account alternative now)
consolidation_proposal.body:
## Problem / why
A worker session can read/write files ANYWHERE on the machine - there is no enforced boundary at the session's
own working folder. During BI-PF-1325 a session amended a backlog item (BI-PF-1325) that exists only in ANOTHER
checkout (PF-features) by writing that checkout's file directly (the item was not present in the session's own
folder). All sessions currently run under ONE OS account, so filesystem ACLs cannot separate them today.

## Goal & value
A session can only affect its OWN working folder: cross-folder writes are prevented (long-term, hard) or at least
detected + reverted + escalated (now).

## In scope
- LONG-TERM (HARD): per-session OS identity (dedicated user / container / Windows AppContainer) whose ACL grants
  write ONLY inside the session's worktree; sibling folders read-only/denied. Requires a per-session identity.
- NOW (single account) - session-scope guard:
  (a) declare the session root (the worker worktree) via env (e.g. PF_SESSION_ROOT);
  (b) fail-closed on every PF/WorkerGrid-mediated write whose target is outside the root;
  (c) a git hook that refuses staged paths outside the root;
  (d) a filesystem watchdog that detects writes outside the root, reverts them, and raises an issue.
- Charter/AGENTS rule: never write/delete outside your own working folder.

## Out of scope
- Provisioning multiple OS users (environment setup; enables the long-term hard guard).

## Approach
Reuse existing owners (pre-commit/pre-push hooks, wired_audit, the WorkerGrid launcher); add a session-guard
module wired into the worker launcher + the write paths; design the ACL path now, implement it once a
per-session identity exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- A PF/WorkerGrid-mediated write outside the session root is refused; a raw-shell write is detected + reverted +
  an issue raised (watchdog).
- The pre-commit/pre-push hook fails on out-of-root staged paths.
- The rule is documented; the long-term ACL design is recorded.

## Risks
- A raw shell/file call bypasses an in-agent guard (soft) -> mitigated by the ACL long-term.
- Watchdog detect-after-write window -> documented.

## Open question (needs a design decision BEFORE implementing)
No per-session OS identity exists today (one account runs all sessions), so an ACL-per-user hard guard is NOT
possible yet. The "hard now" options must be reviewed/decided:
- container per session (WSL2/Docker) with ONLY the worktree bind-mounted RW (write elsewhere -> EPERM), or
- Windows AppContainer + a filesystem capability granting write only to the worktree.
Decide which (and how) before coding; ACL-per-user becomes the hard guard once sessions get their own identity.

## Related
Issue IS-PF-0050; IS-PF-0036 (one working tree per session).

consolidation_proposal.title: Session isolation guard: never write outside the session's own working folder (hard ACL long-term + single-account alternative now)
consolidation_proposal.body:
## Problem / why
A worker session can read/write files ANYWHERE on the machine - there is no enforced boundary at the session's
own working folder. During BI-PF-1325 a session amended a backlog item (BI-PF-1325) that exists only in ANOTHER
checkout (PF-features) by writing that checkout's file directly (the item was not present in the session's own
folder). All sessions currently run under ONE OS account, so filesystem ACLs cannot separate them today.

## Goal & value
A session can only affect its OWN working folder: cross-folder writes are prevented (long-term, hard) or at least
detected + reverted + escalated (now).

## In scope
- LONG-TERM (HARD): per-session OS identity (dedicated user / container / Windows AppContainer) whose ACL grants
  write ONLY inside the session's worktree; sibling folders read-only/denied. Requires a per-session identity.
- NOW (single account) - session-scope guard:
  (a) declare the session root (the worker worktree) via env (e.g. PF_SESSION_ROOT);
  (b) fail-closed on every PF/WorkerGrid-mediated write whose target is outside the root;
  (c) a git hook that refuses staged paths outside the root;
  (d) a filesystem watchdog that detects writes outside the root, reverts them, and raises an issue.
- Charter/AGENTS rule: never write/delete outside your own working folder.

## Out of scope
- Provisioning multiple OS users (environment setup; enables the long-term hard guard).

## Approach
Reuse existing owners (pre-commit/pre-push hooks, wired_audit, the WorkerGrid launcher); add a session-guard
module wired into the worker launcher + the write paths; design the ACL path now, implement it once a
per-session identity exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- A PF/WorkerGrid-mediated write outside the session root is refused; a raw-shell write is detected + reverted +
  an issue raised (watchdog).
- The pre-commit/pre-push hook fails on out-of-root staged paths.
- The rule is documented; the long-term ACL design is recorded.

## Risks
- A raw shell/file call bypasses an in-agent guard (soft) -> mitigated by the ACL long-term.
- Watchdog detect-after-write window -> documented.

## Open question (needs a design decision BEFORE implementing)
No per-session OS identity exists today (one account runs all sessions), so an ACL-per-user hard guard is NOT
possible yet. The "hard now" options must be reviewed/decided:
- container per session (WSL2/Docker) with ONLY the worktree bind-mounted RW (write elsewhere -> EPERM), or
- Windows AppContainer + a filesystem capability granting write only to the worktree.
Decide which (and how) before coding; ACL-per-user becomes the hard guard once sessions get their own identity.
